# Oxide

> Oxide is a free, open-source desktop terminal app that knows your GitHub Projects: open a Project, open as many clean terminals as you like in its folder, and run whatever you want in them, with the Project's Issues, pull requests and files at hand.

This file is contributor-facing: architecture, ADRs, and the CI and release process. User-facing docs (install, quick start, concepts, FAQ) live in the website's [llms.txt](https://oxide.cavallinilorenzo.com/llms.txt).

Oxide does not know about agents: a terminal is a plain shell, so an agent CLI is just a command typed in it. It has no telemetry. It is built with Rust and Tauri 2, for macOS (Apple Silicon), Windows and Linux.

Key facts:

- Repository: https://github.com/getoxide/oxide
- License: MIT. Status: pre-release (version 0.x). Downloads: https://github.com/getoxide/oxide/releases
- Stack: Rust core (`crates/oxide-core`), platform layer and process primitives (`crates/oxide-platform`), thin Tauri shell (`crates/oxide-app`), React/TypeScript webview (`web/`), Monaco editor, xterm terminal, SQLite storage.
- Requirements: `git`; optionally the GitHub CLI `gh`.
